scope: Durable cycle-level reading language. Computed chapter grammar, phase geometry, nameability, chart contacts, seed echoes, and event comparisons do not live here.

readings.title: The civilizational substrate
readings.summary: This clock tracks the deep field in which a society decides what is real, valuable, and imaginable enough to build.
readings.authority_question: Which picture of reality becomes infrastructure, and who acquires the power to make that picture feel inevitable?
readings.constructive: A shared imaginative field can carry technologies and institutions that enlarge human agency across generations.
readings.shadow: The same field can naturalize mass persuasion, abstraction, and systems so large that no one appears responsible for them.
readings.continuity: Old civilizational habits can absorb new tools without surrendering the authority arrangement beneath them.

readings.title: Revolutionary imagination enters the structure
readings.summary: This clock follows the meeting of rupture and vision: the future is imagined, networked, dissolved, and made culturally thinkable.
readings.authority_question: Who translates a liberating vision into the operating assumptions of the next order?
readings.constructive: Rigid institutions can loosen while new networks distribute knowledge, creativity, and participation.
readings.shadow: Freedom can be simulated through spectacle, digital dependency, or ideals that dissolve accountability faster than hierarchy.
readings.continuity: An institution may adopt revolutionary language and tools while preserving its old command structure.

readings.title: Technical revolution meets concentrated power
readings.summary: This clock follows deep power moving through invention, infrastructure, and the repeated struggle between liberation and control.
readings.authority_question: Does technical power widen the field of decision, or centralize it behind systems few people can inspect?
readings.constructive: Obsolete concentrations of power can break, allowing new actors and capacities to enter the field.
readings.shadow: Revolutionary tools can produce more total forms of surveillance, coercion, and unaccountable private power.
readings.continuity: The owners may change while the deeper pattern—power accumulating around scarce infrastructure—remains intact.

readings.title: Institution meets rupture
readings.summary: This clock tests whether an established order can incorporate the breakthrough without either freezing or flying apart.
readings.authority_question: Which innovations become lawful and durable, and who controls the gate between experiment and institution?
readings.constructive: Reform can give a real innovation standards, continuity, and public legitimacy.
readings.shadow: Authority can suppress change, or weaponize disruption to install a harsher structure under the banner of freedom.
readings.continuity: A managed update can preserve the incumbent settlement while changing its visible machinery.

readings.title: Law meets the ideal
readings.summary: This clock asks what happens when a collective dream seeks a body—and when an institution loses the story that justified it.
readings.authority_question: Which ideal receives law, budget, office, and enforcement—and what must remain unresolved for the structure to hold?
readings.constructive: Vision can become a humane institution with boundaries strong enough to endure and flexible enough to serve.
readings.shadow: Fog can become policy: undefined mandates, moral theater, sacrifice without accountability, or authority justified by emergency feeling.
readings.continuity: A new ideal can re-enchant an old apparatus without changing who decides or how decisions become binding.

readings.title: State power under compression
readings.summary: This clock follows authority when survival, coercion, scarcity, and institutional regeneration are forced into the same chamber.
readings.authority_question: What power is claimed as necessary, who can constrain it, and what survives the restructuring as legitimate authority?
readings.constructive: A failing institution can confront corruption, discard dead weight, and rebuild around duties it can actually carry.
readings.shadow: Crisis can legitimate concentrated force, punitive austerity, secrecy, and permanent emergency machinery.
readings.continuity: A visible restructuring can remove personnel while leaving the underlying coercive architecture untouched.

readings.title: Scale meets restraint
readings.summary: This clock follows the public settlement between expansion and limit: what a society authorizes, funds, teaches, and expects to last.
readings.authority_question: Which promises receive institutional form, and which limits are treated as legitimate rather than merely obstructive?
readings.constructive: Growth can be disciplined into durable law, finance, and public capacity.
readings.shadow: Expansion can serve incumbents while austerity disciplines everyone else, producing legitimacy without reciprocity.
readings.continuity: The system can alternate stimulus and restraint while keeping the same beneficiaries and decision rules.

readings.title: The breakthrough seeks legitimacy
readings.summary: This clock follows rapid openings—technical, political, intellectual—and the attempt to scale them into a new common sense.
readings.authority_question: Who is permitted to call a rupture progress, and who gains standing when the breakthrough is normalized?
readings.constructive: A real opening can spread knowledge, opportunity, and institutional alternatives faster than gatekeepers can contain it.
readings.shadow: Novelty can be over-sold, captured by capital, or used to evade safeguards before consequences are visible.
readings.continuity: A celebrated innovation may extend the current order more efficiently rather than replace it.

readings.title: Belief becomes a public force
readings.summary: This clock amplifies ideals, stories, faith, and projection until they can move markets, institutions, and collective permission.
readings.authority_question: Which story acquires public trust, and what evidence is demanded before inspiration becomes policy?
readings.constructive: A generous vision can enlarge solidarity and make previously unthinkable coordination possible.
readings.shadow: Inflated belief can outrun facts, finance fantasy, or turn moral yearning into cover for diffuse authority.
readings.continuity: New rhetoric can refresh public faith while leaving operative rules and material control unchanged.

readings.title: Expansion confronts power
readings.summary: This clock brings scale, wealth, law, and legitimacy into direct contact with concentrated power and its claim to necessity.
readings.authority_question: Who gets to enlarge the field of action, by what authority, and who can refuse the terms of that expansion?
readings.constructive: Large resources can be mobilized to expose corruption, reform captured systems, or build capacity equal to the problem.
readings.shadow: Power can magnify itself through finance, ideology, enforcement, and the insistence that scale alone proves legitimacy.
readings.continuity: The contest can redistribute influence among elites without changing the public's actual power to decide.
